title.narrative: Organisational Development Planning for African Initiatives

description.narrative: AI exists to tackle injustice and poverty. AI support the rights of people to take part in the social, economic, political and environmental decision-making that affects them at a community, national and international level. AI’s work focuses on girls' education, women’s rights, sustainable livelihoods, land rights and economic empowerment. They work in long-term partnership, strengthening the capacity of grassroots organisations in Tanzania and Ghana through the provision of information, resources, training, advice, mentoring for staff, monitoring and evaluation and support our partners to measure impact. As a growing organisation, it is necessary for AI to plan more effectively for the future in order to support the identified needs of our partners and implement effective programmes. This grant would allow AI to undertake a full organisational assessment and develop a capacity plan that would strengthen AI to more effectively achieve its goals and implement effective programmes both overseas and in the UK. The inclusive approach would help AI to identify and prioritise key organisational needs and plan and apply appropriate internal capacity building activities. Through undertaking stimulating reflection, learning, and dialogue, new and old problems and opportunities will be examined, and ideas for addressing them will be generated.
